title: Stargardt Disease: The ABCA4 Retinopathy Masterclass
summary: Stargardt Disease (STGD1) is the most common inherited juvenile macular dystrophy, characterized by the accumulation of lipofuscin (A2E) within the RPE due to mutations in the ABCA4 gene. This guide provides a deep dive into the clinical findings, the pathognomonic 'dark choroid' on FFA, and current management protocols for residents and fellows.

sections.title: Pathophysiology: The Retinoid Cycle Failure
content: Step 1: Defective ABCA4 protein fails to transport all-trans-retinal out of the photoreceptor disc.
Step 2: Accumulation of N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine (PE).
Step 3: Conversion into toxic bis-retinoid A2E within the RPE lysosomal system.
Step 4: RPE cell death due to lysosomal membrane rupture and oxidative stress.
Step 5: Secondary secondary degeneration of overlying photoreceptors (Macular Atrophy).

rows: Pigmentary changes at fovea; No flecks within 1 DD of fovea

Extensive flecks and RPE atrophy; Beaten-bronze macula
Diffusely resorbed flecks; Extensive chorioretinal atrophy

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Beaten-Bronze Macula: Snail-slime appearance of the fovea.
Pisciform Flecks: Yellow-white, fish-tail shaped subretinal deposits at the level of RPE.
Sparing of the Peripapillary RPE: Often seen in ABCA4-related STGD1.
Bull’s Eye Maculopathy: Late stage appearance of RPE atrophy.
Salt and Pepper Pigmentary Changes: In the peripheral retina of advanced cases.

Earlier color vision loss, severe photophobia

sections.title: Diagnostic Imaging Workup
content: Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Hyper-AF flecks (active) and Hypo-AF areas (RPE atrophy).
Fluorescein Angiogram (FFA): Look for 'Silent/Dark Choroid' (80% sensitive) due to lipofuscin blocking choroidal flush.
Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): Loss of Ellipsoid Zone (EZ), RPE thinning, and 'outer retinal tubulations' in late stages.
Electrophysiology: Full-field ERG to determine prognostic category (Group I, II, or III).
Genetic Testing: Confirmation of biallelic ABCA4 mutations.

sections.title: CRITICAL CONTRAINDICATION
content: DO NOT supplement with Vitamin A / Beta-carotene.
Vitamin A fuels the visual cycle and accelerates A2E accumulation/toxicity.
Avoid AREDS formulations containing Vitamin A in these patients.

content.explanation: S: Silent Choroid on FFA; T: Toxic A2E accumulation; A: ABCA4 Mutation (Recessive); R: RPE Flecks (Pisciform); G: Genetics (1p22).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Boards
content: The 'Silent Choroid' occurs because lipofuscin absorbs the blue light of the FFA, preventing visualization of the choroidal flush.
Stargardt is the most common cause of a childhood macular dystrophy.
Vision loss often precedes visible ophthalmoscopic findings ('Phenotype-Genotype lag').
Peripapillary sparing is a hallmark that differentiates STGD1 from other dystrophies.

sections.title: Management & Low Vision Strategy
content: 1. Confirm diagnosis via genetic testing (ABCA4) and multimodal imaging.
2. Counseling: Explain the recessive inheritance (25% risk for siblings).
3. Protection: Prescribe UV-blocking and Blue-light blocking sunglasses (may slow A2E formation).
4. Nutrition: Advise against Vitamin A; emphasize lutein/zeaxanthin and Omega-3s.
5. Low Vision: Refer early for magnifiers, telescopic lenses, and school/workplace accommodations.
6. Clinical Trials: Monitor for Gene Therapy (SAR422451) or pharmacological trials (e.g., Emixustat).

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Recent Advances
sections.content: The ProgStar Study (Natural History of the Progression of Stargardt Disease) provided critical longitudinal data on lesion growth (atrophy) using FAF. Recent research focuses on 'Visual Cycle Modulators' (like ALK-001, a deuterated Vitamin A) which aim to slow down the dimerization of Vitamin A into toxic A2E without causing night blindness. Gene therapy trials using Lentiviral vectors are ongoing due to the large size of the ABCA4 gene (cDNA ~6.8kb), which exceeds standard AAV capacity.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Suspect Rapid Progression
content: Rapid expansion of scotoma on Goldmann visual fields.
Development of Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV) - Rare but possible.
Significant reduction in scotopic ERG amplitudes (indicates rod involvement).
Sudden metamorphopsia (requires immediate OCT to rule out CNV).
